# Toast

Toast markup, configuration, behavior, and usage example. An ephemeral, auto-dismissing message shown one at a time (e.g. "saved", "error"). Split from Notification, which is a persistent, manually-dismissed panel: the toast is the same card, only one at a time and timed, in its own fixed container. Both are the shared alert card underneath (see Alerts): this component only manages the single floating stack and the countdown bar around it. Full JSON field list is under @pgs-data "toast"; full JS options list is under each @api method below. The JSON form and the JS options now use the same names; the previous message, title-close and duration keys are still accepted as aliases. Two custom events are dispatched, owned by the shared alert engine: pgs:alert:buttonClick on a buttons[] element when clicked (detail: id, buttonId, type, title, description, link; cancelable — call event.preventDefault() to stop the navigation), and pgs:alert:close on the toast element right before it is removed, whether by the dismiss button or by its own timeout (detail: id, type, title, description).

## PGS

- `toastLoad`: creates one toast from a JSON object on page load; see @pgs-data "toast" for every accepted field. Its options, like toastLoad['toastRight'], are applied to the container for that toast.
- `toastExe`: creates one toast from a JSON object each time the element is clicked; same fields and options as toastLoad.
- `toast`: write it yourself, bare like this, to place the container elsewhere; the module leaves it alone and never generates a second one. Leave it empty, because its content is replaced at every toast.

## PGS generated by JavaScript

- `_toast`: the container the toasts are shown in, appended at the end of the body when no toast was written by hand. It also carries, for the toast being shown, the options written on its trigger.

## PGS Options (component brackets)

- `toastLeft`: shows the toast against the left edge instead of the centre. Write it on toastLoad or toastExe, or pass it in the position option of pgs.toast: the JavaScript copies it to the container, for that toast only.
- `toastRight`: the same, against the right edge.
- `toastCenter`: the same, in the middle of the screen.
- `toastBottom`: the same, against the bottom edge instead of the top.

## PGS Data

- `toast`: JSON object read by toastLoad/toastExe on page load or click; a new toast replaces whatever is currently shown — every field, with its accepted values and its default, is annotated in the reference below.

## JavaScript API

- `pgs.toast.init(root)`: scans root for toastLoad and toastExe and initializes them; runs automatically on page load and again via pgs.init(root) for content added later.
- `pgs.toast.trigger(root)`: alias of pgs.toast.init(root).
- `pgs.toast.error(optionsOrTitle)`: a title string, or an options object — see the full field reference in the commented example below.
- `pgs.toast.success(optionsOrTitle)`: a title string, or an options object — see the full field reference in the commented example below.
- `pgs.toast.info(optionsOrTitle)`: a title string, or an options object — see the full field reference in the commented example below.
- `pgs.toast.warning(optionsOrTitle)`: a title string, or an options object — see the full field reference in the commented example below.
- `pgs.toast.neutral(optionsOrTitle)`: the plain toast, same arguments as the others; it has no title or glyph of its own, so pass at least a description.
- `pgs.toast.deleteAll()`: removes the currently shown toast, if any.

## Related elements

### PGS

- `hidden`: uses the related hidden component or utility in this example.
- `button`: uses the related button component or utility in this example.

### Other

- `alerts`: owns the card itself and the engine that builds it (icon, content, dismiss button, action buttons, timeout, events — see its own @pgs-generated for every _alert* token); this component only manages the fixed stacking container and the countdown bar around it.
- `neutral`: the plain severity option owned by Alerts; no colour, no glyph and no title of its own, so the card stays on the box surface.
- `success`: the success severity option owned by Alerts.
- `error`: the error severity option owned by Alerts.
- `warning`: the warning severity option owned by Alerts.
- `info`: the info severity option owned by Alerts.
- `icon`: draws the glyph that marks the toast type; see Icon for the whole set.
- `icon-circleXmark`: the glyph of the error type.
- `icon-circleCheck`: the glyph of the success type.
- `icon-circleInfo`: the glyph of the info type.
- `icon-triangleExclamation`: the glyph of the warning type.
- `icon-close`: the cross the dismiss button draws.
- `btnIconOnly`: shapes that dismiss button as an icon-only button; see Button.

## Output

Complete HTML markup and usage example for Toast.

## PGS Data fields

```html
pgs-data='toast[{
    "title": "",                    // omitted falls back to the title of the type
    "description": "",              // plain text under the title; a newline becomes a line break
    "type": "info",                 // neutral | error | success | warning | info, and anything else falls back to info
    "icon": null,                   // HTML string; null uses the icon of the type
    "timeout": 4000,                // milliseconds before it dismisses itself; a value that is not a number is ignored
    "closeTitle": "Close"           // accessible name of the dismiss button, which always draws a cross
    "buttons": [                    // omitted or empty leaves only the dismiss button; same shape as Notification
        {  
            "id": null,             // reported as buttonId by pgs:alert:buttonClick
            "title": "",            // label of the button
            "link": null,           // navigates there; omit it to only dispatch the event
            "close": true,          // dismisses the toast after the click; false keeps it, e.g. for a link
            "optionButton": null    // pgs-data token added to the button, e.g. btnMini
        }
    ],
}]'
```


## JavaScript Usage

```js
pgs.toast.success({
    title: "",
    description: "",
    icon: null,
    timeout: 4000,
    buttons: [
        { 
            id: undefined, 
            title: "", 
            link: undefined, 
            close: true, 
            optionButton: undefined 
        }
    ],
    closeTitle: "Close",
    position: []            // toastLeft | toastRight | toastCenter | toastBottom, alone or together, e.g. ["toastLeft", "toastBottom"]; for this toast only
});
```

## Trigger

### toastExe

Shows the toast described in its pgs-data each time the element is clicked. A new toast replaces the one still on screen.

```html
<button pgs="button toastExe" pgs-data='toast[{
    "title": "Benvenuto",
    "description": "Message",
    "type": "success",
    "icon": null,
    "timeout": "7000",
    "buttons": [{ "title": "Open", "link": "#", "close": true }],
    "closeTitle": "Close"
}]'> Trigger Toast</button>
```

### toastLoad

Shows the toast described in its pgs-data once, when the page loads. The element is hidden and consumed: nothing of it stays in the page.

```html
<div pgs="hidden toastLoad" pgs-data='toast[{
        "title": "Benvenuto",
        "description": "Message",
        "type": "neutral",
        "icon": "<img src=\"../assets/img/logo.svg\" alt=\"\">",
        "timeout": "7000",
        "closeTitle": "Close"
    }]'></div>
```

## Position

### Left

toastLeft on the trigger shows that toast against the left edge instead of the centre. The JavaScript copies it to the container for that toast only, so the next one starts again from its own options.

```html
<button pgs="button toastExe['toastLeft']" pgs-data='toast[{
    "title": "On the left",
    "description": "Against the left edge.",
    "type": "info",
    "timeout": "7000"
}]'>Toast on the left</button>
```

### Right

The same, against the right edge, with toastRight.

```html
<button pgs="button toastExe['toastRight']" pgs-data='toast[{
    "title": "On the right",
    "description": "Against the right edge.",
    "type": "info",
    "timeout": "7000"
}]'>Toast on the right</button>
```

### Center

toastCenter puts the toast in the middle of the screen.

```html
<button pgs="button toastExe['toastCenter']" pgs-data='toast[{
    "title": "In the middle",
    "description": "Centred on the screen.",
    "type": "info",
    "timeout": "7000"
}]'>Toast in the center</button>
```

### Bottom

toastBottom moves the toast to the bottom edge, instead of under the header.

```html
<button pgs="button toastExe['toastBottom']" pgs-data='toast[{
    "title": "At the bottom",
    "description": "Against the bottom edge.",
    "type": "info",
    "timeout": "7000"
}]'>Toast at the bottom</button>
```
